description: TinyDispatcher is a small, compile-time oriented dispatcher for .NET with pipelines and source generation.
releaseNotes:
Performance: optimized middleware pipeline execution (significantly reduced allocations in the dispatch path). Breaking: middleware contract updated (see migration below).

Pipeline Hardening & Performance Refactor (Breaking Changes)

This prerelease delivers a major redesign of the TinyDispatcher pipeline execution model. Generated pipelines are now switch-runner based with constructor-injected middleware, reducing allocations and improving readability of the generated code.

What changed

  • Replaced delegate-chaining pipelines with switch-based generated pipelines (runtime runner).
  • Middleware is now constructor-injected into generated pipelines (DI-friendly, more readable code).
  • Deterministic middleware layering is enforced consistently: Global → Policy → Per-command → Handler.
  • Benchmarks updated and validated in Release mode.

Breaking changes (Middleware API)

CommandDelegate has been removed and middleware now uses a runtime interface.

Old signature:

            Task InvokeAsync(
            TCommand command,
            TContext context,
            CommandDelegate next,
            CancellationToken ct);

New signature:

            ValueTask InvokeAsync(
            TCommand command,
            TContext context,
            Pipeline.ICommandPipelineRuntime runtime,
            CancellationToken ct);

Migration guide

Replace:

            await next(command, context, ct);

With:

            await runtime.NextAsync(command, context, ct);

If your middleware only forwards execution:

            public ValueTask InvokeAsync(
            TCommand command,
            TContext context,
            Pipeline.ICommandPipelineRuntime runtime,
            CancellationToken ct)
            => runtime.NextAsync(command, context, ct);

Pipeline Contract Simplification (Breaking)

The dispatcher no longer performs runtime pipeline precedence resolution. Global, Policy, and Per-command pipelines are now unified under a single ICommandPipeline contract.

What changed

  • Removed IPolicyCommandPipeline<,>.
  • Removed IGlobalCommandPipeline<,>.
  • Dispatcher now resolves a single ICommandPipeline.
  • Pipeline precedence (Per-command → Policy → Global) is enforced at compile-time by source generation.
  • Reduced DI lookups and removed runtime branching in the dispatch path.

Migration guide

If you were implementing IPolicyCommandPipeline<,> or IGlobalCommandPipeline<,>, replace them with ICommandPipeline.

Notes

  • This change simplifies the public API surface and reduces runtime complexity.
  • Pipeline resolution is now deterministic and fully generator-driven.
  • This is part of the final hardening phase toward v1.0.
